# Lessons from Prompt Box

Prompt Box was the first app built from the original scaffold: a voice
dictation tool on top of whisper.cpp, egui, and OpenAI, built over two days
with an AI coding agent. These are the things that made it go well, in the
order they mattered. The template bakes in the ones that can be baked in.

## Architecture

**Put a deterministic core behind an action/effect boundary from day one.**
The scaffold started with logic as plain methods on the app struct. The
first real feature (streaming speech with provisional text) made it clear
that a state machine with explicit inputs (`AppAction`), explicit outputs
(`Effect`), and an injected `Clock` was the only way to test timing
behavior without sleeping. Every later feature slotted into that shape:
voice commands, AI rewrites on worker threads, tool plugins, toasts. Around
ninety core tests ran in well under a second. The template ships this
shape with one trivial feature in it so the pattern is there to copy.

**Ports and adapters earn their keep on the second adapter.** Clipboard,
file store, speech engine, typist, rewriter: each got a trait, a real
implementation, and a fake. The fakes made headless UI tests possible on
CI and let the whole app run in a "Debug" mode with scripted dictation and
no model. Write the fake at the same time as the real adapter, in the same
file.

**Keep `ui.rs` dumb.** Edit diffing and keyboard shortcuts were the only
logic that had to live near egui, and even those produce actions. When a
bug showed up, it was almost always reproducible as a core test.

## Process

**Spike risky technology in a throwaway crate first.** Before Milestone 1,
a standalone `spikes/voice-spike` crate answered whether whisper.cpp could
stream on this machine, what the real API looked like, and how long the
first Metal shader compile takes. Its README recorded the findings. The
spike's fixtures were reused as test inputs later.

**Milestones, each a working app.** Shell, then microphone, then editing
operations, then voice commands, then AI, then projects. Each milestone was
one commit with the README updated. Scope stayed honest because the app
had to run at every step.

**Write the design doc, then stop consulting it.** A product design doc
set priorities ("never silently lose speech" first). It was useful for
ordering milestones and for the layering diagram in `lib.rs`. Beyond that
the code and README became the source of truth, and the doc was left as
history.

**Pre-commit hook plus CI, both running the same three commands.** Nothing
formatted wrong, lint-dirty, or failing ever landed. The hook never modifies
files; it just says no. Clippy pedantic caught real mistakes and taught
idioms along the way. The two `allow`s in `Cargo.toml` are the only lints
that were pure noise.

**Audit comments once features settle.** Halfway through, a pass removed
comments that restated the code or narrated which milestone added what.
The rule since: comments say why.

## Tooling facts that cost time

- egui 0.36 renamed the `App` trait method to `ui`, merged panels into one
  `Panel` type, and kittest needs `.focus()` before `type_text`. See
  `CLAUDE.md`. When docs and compiler disagree, read the crate source in
  `~/.cargo/registry`.
- eframe 0.36 runs `App::logic`, not `App::ui`, while the window is
  occluded or minimized; anything that must keep ticking belongs in
  `logic`. The symptom looked like a sleep bug: the control port went
  silent until the window was uncovered.
- The crate forbids `unsafe`, and that survived native AppKit calls
  (Dock badge) because `objc2` exposes safe wrappers for the common
  methods. Put such code in a tiny `cfg`-gated adapter.
- macOS ties the Accessibility grant to the code signature, so an ad-hoc
  signed app loses the grant on every rebuild. A self-signed "Code Signing"
  certificate fixes it. The bundle script and README in Prompt Box have the
  recipe.
- A bundled `.app` starts with `/` as its working directory, so reading a
  `.env` from the current directory silently fails. Read secrets from a
  settings file in the platform data directory instead, with `.env` as a
  dev-only fallback.
- Two monitors: `screencapture -x a.png b.png` captures both; one path
  only gives the primary display.
- Linux CI for eframe needs `libxkbcommon-dev libgtk-3-dev libssl-dev`;
  audio adds `libasound2-dev`, whisper adds `cmake`.

## The path the issue describes

"Review stage" here is a *workflow* stage: a plan review run by Switchboard, with `AttemptKind::Workflow`. It is not the code review in `dispatch/src/review.rs`. That stage has its own carry-over logic (`carry_source`, `review.rs:3608`), which is what the issue's expectation resembles. Plan review has none.

1. `workflow_stage` (`dispatch/src/scheduler.rs:7379`) picks the stage's next move per context. For a failed latest attempt with an acted `rerun` answer (`may_rerun`, `:10665`) it calls `start_workflow` with `next_n`. With no attempt it starts attempt 1 the same way.
2. `start_workflow` (`:7436`) takes the plan via `review_subject(t, &subject)` (`:7457`). It copies that file to `<ticket dir>/<stage>/<n>/<ctx>/<subject>.md` (`attempt_dir`, `:6303`; the copy is at `:7471`). It passes the file as `Body::WorkflowStart { source, plan: copy, ... }` (`:7510`).
3. `review_subject` (`:10534`) walks `t.attempts` newest first. It keeps only `AttemptState::Complete` attempts and takes the first whose `artifacts` has the subject name. It returns that path and that attempt's `session`.
   - After a failed review/1, the newest Complete attempt with a `plan` artifact is the plan stage's attempt. Its file is `plan/1/joined/plan.md`.
   - A failed review attempt's copy is never considered, whatever the planner wrote into it.
   - `source` is the plan stage's session, the original planner. The app clones that planner for the new run. The clone never saw the owner's `revise` note or the revised plan.
4. This explains the repro. The `revise` edits happen in place on `review/1/.../plan.md`, and only a `Finalized`/`HandedOff` run sets `AttemptState::Complete` (`poll_workflow`, around `:7843`).
   - `Ticket::input_where` (`dispatch/src/ticket.rs:1437-1462`) is the same Complete-only rule. It is deliberate: "an agent is handed `input_where`'s complete files".
   - `Ticket::shown_where` (`:1467-1488`) also accepts an open workflow attempt, but not a failed one. So a failed review/1 drops out of `show`'s plan too.
5. A `revise` (`scheduler.rs:7565`) does these things:
   - The note goes into the decision as `DecisionState::Answered { note, by, acted }`.
   - It writes `<subject>.feedback-<round>.md` beside the reviewed copy, headed `OWNER_ROUND_HEADING` (`dispatch/src/lib.rs:96`).
   - It pushes a `Revision { round, by, at_ms }` onto `Attempt.revisions` (`ticket.rs:350`).
   - It sends `Body::WorkflowObject { run, round, text }` to Switchboard, which has the planner clone revise the copy and write `<subject>.response-<round>.md`.

   So the owner's note survives on disk in three places: the decision, the feedback file and `revisions`. The revised plan is only in the copy file. The attempt-2 copy is made fresh from `plan/1` and never reads these.
6. A failure `no such run` comes from `poll_workflow` (`:7761`, `NO_SUCH_RUN` at `:8445`) and calls `fail_attempt`.
   - `fail_attempt_with` (`:7195`) sets `AttemptState::Failed`, asks `rerun`/`park` or parks past `max_reruns`.
   - It does not touch the copy or the round files.
   - The `rerun` answer goes through `act_on_answers` (`:3524`) and `retire_replaced` (`:3578`), which kills processes and (if the owner gave a note) records a rework note. A workflow stage has no use of it.
7. `rerun_ask` (`:9335`) builds the question ("failed: <reason>. Run it again?" plus `rerun_carries`, `:9382`). `rerun_carries` says something only for code review attempts and returns "" for workflow attempts. That is where a "this rerun will review plan/1 / review/1" sentence would go.
8. Nothing is checked on the rerun for a stage whose failed attempt had `revisions`. No test covers revise-then-failed-run-then-rerun. Neighbouring tests:
   - `a_failed_review_run_fails_the_attempt_and_a_rerun_starts_a_new_run` (`dispatch/tests/first_slice.rs:3257`) uses `at_review_run` (`:3231`) and `review_run_fails` (`:3249`);
   - the revise tests at `:3417-3600` (`revise` helper `:3417`, `at_finalize`);
   - unit tests at `scheduler.rs:12449` and about `:12850-12868` (which plan a reader is given while a review is open or complete);
   - `ticket.rs:1800-1870` (`input` vs `shown`);
   - `serve.rs:1380-1710` (paths).

## `show`'s `files:` block

- `show` is `dispatch/src/main.rs:~935` (`fn show`; `files:` at `:981`). It calls `print_lane_files("plan", &p.plan_files)` (`:896`).
- It prints `  plan: <path>` and, only when `LaneFile.reviewing`, `(reviewed copy, round N, review open)`.
- `ticket_paths` (`dispatch/src/serve.rs:~538`) builds `plan_files` from `shown_lane_files` (`scheduler.rs:~10900`, `lane_files_by`). That is one file per lane, or one file in all, from `Ticket::shown_where`. So only one `plan.md` is ever listed, and prior copies and revisions never appear.
- `LaneFile` is in `dispatch-control` (`PathsView.plan_files`, `plan_stage`, `plan_reviewed`, `plan_reviewing`, `plan_round`). It is a wire type; CLAUDE.md says extend additively and bump versions if a serialized `model.rs` type changes. The app (`src/ui/ticket.rs:~427`) and the Swift client (`client/Sources/SwitchboardProtocol/Tickets.swift`) read it.
- `plan_rounds` (`serve.rs:~504`) takes the *latest* workflow attempt with artifacts for the round list, so after a rerun, attempt 1's rounds and revision are not listed either.
- `show`'s attempts list ("review/1 joined failed") is `print_attempts`; it does not mention the revised copy.

## On-disk record and rehydration (before the pane)

- Source of truth: the ticket record (`Ticket.attempts[]`, `Attempt.artifacts`, `.revisions`, `.run`, `.session`, `.state`; `decisions[]` with `Answered { note, by, acted }`) in Dispatch's data dir, written atomically via `save_ticket`. The plan files live under `<data>/tickets/<id>/<stage>/<n>/<ctx>/`.
- Rehydration of a rerun is a pure function of those records: `workflow_stage` re-reads the ticket on every pass; `review_subject` re-derives the plan file from `attempts`. A restart mid-rerun re-derives the same source. A fix that only changes `review_subject`'s choice needs no new record field: the failed attempt's `artifacts[subject]` plus a non-empty `revisions` is enough to say "this copy holds an owner revision". If the fix instead stores a "carried from review/1" marker on the new attempt (as code review does with `Attempt.carried_from`), that is a serialized `Attempt` field: `#[serde(default)]`, a `RECORD_VERSION` bump and a migration step (CLAUDE.md "Extending the contract"; the code review carry bumped dispatch `RECORD_VERSION` to 4).
- In the app (Switchboard), the run itself is a `WorkflowRun` record with `plan` path, `planner` and `reviewer` sessions, rounds and snapshots (design.md 1000-1060). A new `workflow.start` creates a new run; the old run's planner clone and its context are not reused.
- Pane: `show` text, the app's ticket Plan tab ("Reviewed copy, round N: review open", design.md ~2161), and the rerun question text. All are derived from the above.

## What I did not check

- Whether the Switchboard app (the `src/` side) deletes or alters a failed run's plan copy or round files when the run is retired.
- Whether the reviewed copy at a failed attempt can be mid-edit (the planner clone writing it when the run died).
- The Swift client and the app UI handling of more than one `plan.md`.
- `dispatch/src/report.rs`, `history.rs`, `recover.rs`, `restart.rs` for other users of `review_subject`/`input("plan")`. I did not run grep for other call sites of `review_subject` beyond `start_workflow`.
- Nothing was built or run; no tests executed.

## Open questions

- [tree] Which other call sites read the plan through `Ticket::input`/`input_where` or `review_subject` (reports, resume, restart, `lane_plans`, `recover.rs`) and would also need the failed attempt's copy to stand in as "newest plan"?

- [tree] Can a failed attempt's copy be half-written (planner clone mid-round, or an owner round whose objection the app refused and whose file was removed at `scheduler.rs:7650`) and is any record on the attempt (`revisions`, round files, the run's last round) enough to tell a finished revision from a partial one?
- [tree] Is there a rule for a failed review attempt that never had a revise (reviewer died in round 1) so that reusing its copy and reusing `plan/N` give the same text, i.e. does picking the failed copy ever lose or change anything the plan stage had written later (e.g. a plan stage rerun after the review failed, which would make `plan/2` newer than `review/1`)?
- [tree] What does the app side do with `source` on `workflow.start` (clone the session from its transcript at the end, per design.md 1050-1060), and does the planner clone for attempt 2, made from the original planner, contradict a revised copy it is handed, so the plan needs to say the revision and the owner's note travel to the new planner?
- [tree] How do `show --json`, the app's ticket page (`src/ui/ticket.rs:~427`) and the Swift client (`TicketFileView`) use `LaneFile`/`PathsView`, so that adding a "prior revision" file or label is additive for them?
- [run] Does the repro really end at a `Failed` review/1 whose `artifacts["plan"]` still points at the revised copy and whose `revisions` is non-empty (the fake Switchboard in `dispatch/tests/first_slice.rs` can model `no such run` after `revise`; I did not run it)?
- [owner] Was review/1's `plan.md` still the revised text when the owner looked (09:28 vs. the failure), and did the owner's lead decisions exist anywhere besides the `revise` note (that is, is the note the only copy that needs to survive)? Needs the owner's ticket data directory.
